items.name: GitHub internal repositories compromised via malicious VS Code extension
items.summary: GitHub confirmed that attackers associated with TeamPCP compromised employee devices using a malicious VS Code extension and accessed internal repositories.
items.executive_summary: The incident demonstrates continued escalation of developer-focused supply chain attacks targeting IDE extensions and CI/CD trust relationships.
change_summary: GitHub publicly acknowledged internal repository exposure
Scope expanded beyond earlier OSS package incidents
Credential rotation and containment actions completed
items.operational_relevance: Organizations relying on GitHub Actions, VS Code extensions, or shared developer tooling should reassess trust assumptions and token management.
items.details: Attackers reportedly used malicious VS Code extensions to gain access to developer environments and internal repositories.

strategic_view.general: Developer ecosystems are becoming strategic attack surfaces.
strategic_view.geopolitical: Such operations can indirectly impact national digital infrastructure through OSS dependency chains.
strategic_view.business: Software vendors face increasing liability and trust challenges.
strategic_view.research_direction: Monitor IDE extensions, CI/CD compromise techniques, and token theft patterns.

assessment.why_it_matters: The attack shows that IDE-level compromise can bypass many traditional security controls.
assessment.delta_from_previous: This expands prior TeamPCP activity into direct GitHub internal compromise.

sources.title: GitHub confirms being hacked by TeamPCP

items.name: Mass GitHub Actions workflow compromise campaign
items.summary: The Megalodon campaign injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows into thousands of repositories to steal secrets and cloud credentials.
items.executive_summary: The operation highlights increasing automation and scale in CI/CD-focused supply chain attacks.
items.operational_relevance: Organizations should treat CI/CD pipelines as high-value infrastructure and monitor workflow modifications.

assessment.why_it_matters: The campaign demonstrates scalable compromise of modern software delivery infrastructure.
assessment.delta_from_previous: This attack scaled automated workflow compromise significantly beyond prior incidents.

items.name: Kali365 phishing-as-a-service abusing Microsoft device code flow
items.summary: FBI warned that Kali365 operators abuse Microsoft device code flow to steal OAuth access and refresh tokens.
items.executive_summary: OAuth token abuse is increasingly replacing traditional password theft and MFA bypass operations.
items.operational_relevance: Organizations using Microsoft 365 should monitor OAuth grants and device code authentication.
recommended_action: Restrict device code flow where possible

assessment.why_it_matters: OAuth token theft bypasses many MFA-centric security models.
assessment.delta_from_previous: The campaign formalizes OAuth token abuse into a commoditized phishing service.

sources.title: Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service Kit Hijacks Microsoft 365 Access Tokens
